goal: Makes internal fatal-error paths (AbortNode-triggered shutdowns) in validation and block storage return util::Result error info to callers instead of silently signaling only through notification callbacks.
Lets libbitcoinkernel applications detect and handle fatal errors programmatically, without registering for kernel notification callbacks.
reviewability: Ready to review, though it is built on the still-open base PR #25665 and effectively cannot be finished or merged before that lands.
58 force-pushes over 2.5 years reflect constant rebasing against unrelated conflicting PRs, not code instability; the design questions raised so far have been resolved.
agreement: Early Concept ACK with no rationale (Graysonbarton). A design concern about wrapping result types was raised and accepted by the author, who changed the approach (maflcko).
A flush/state inconsistency noted by optout21 was acknowledged and split into a separate merged PR (#35621).
A broad philosophical objection to util::Result as a pattern was raised once with no specifics tied to this PR and no follow-up engagement (purpleKarrot).

The benefit is plumbing for error visibility, not a policy or DoS-resistance change.

result.summary: This PR makes validation and block-storage functions that trigger fatal errors (via AbortNode) return util::Result objects carrying error information, instead of leaving callers to learn about fatal failures only through kernel notification callbacks. It is a pure refactor with no intended behavior change, built on top of the still-open #25665 which adds the util::Result infrastructure this PR depends on. It has been alive for over two years and rebased 58+ times against dozens of intervening validation/blockstorage PRs.
result.problem: libbitcoinkernel application authors currently have no way to learn about fatal internal errors (chainstate corruption, flush failures, block-index failures) except by registering for the kernel notifications interface; ordinary function return values give no indication anything went wrong. This makes robust error handling in kernel-based applications difficult, and is a blocker for using validation code as a standalone library.

open_concerns: purpleKarrot's general objection that util::Result-style error handling is the wrong direction for a codebase where Bitcoin's timing does not require it; raised once, not engaged with further by anyone.
resolved_concerns: maflcko's concern that Result<InterruptResult> wrapping was fragile was addressed by the author changing the type ordering.
optout21's observation of a pre-existing flush/state inconsistency was acknowledged and split off into #35621, which merged.

result.card: This PR (ryanofsky, draft, open since 2024-03-21) makes validation and block-storage functions that trigger fatal internal errors (AbortNode-driven shutdowns) return util::Result objects with error information, instead of only notifying via the kernel notifications interface. The description states the goal directly: 'error handling in libbitcoinkernel application code [is] difficult, because the only way to handle these errors is to register for notification callbacks' - this PR fixes that gap as a behavior-preserving refactor. It touches kernel API surface, block storage/flush paths, validation internals, mempool accept functions, and adds substantial util::Result/util::messages infrastructure, with mechanical fallout across mining, rpc, p2p, and tests call sites. It depends on the still-open #25665 for the underlying util::Result machinery, and has been rebased 58+ times against dozens of conflicting in-flight validation/blockstorage PRs, which explains its age rather than any code defect. Review to date is positive: one early Concept ACK, two substantive design concerns raised and resolved (one split into merged PR #35621), and a single unaddressed general objection to the util::Result pattern that no other reviewer echoed.
